title: Job seeker
summary: A résumé that reads in ten seconds: what you're looking for, your experience as a timeline, selected work, and a way to reach you.

for: People looking for a new role

cards.purpose: What role they want, where, and from when.
Roles as a timeline, newest first.
Two to four case studies with a picture.
How a recruiter gets in touch.

slots.ask: What name do you want at the top of the page?
slots.write: Exactly as they give it. Never shorten or translate it.

slots.ask: In one line, what do you do and for whom?
slots.write: One sentence, at most 120 characters, no hashtags or emoji.

slots.ask: Do you want a place on your profile? A city or region is enough.
slots.write: As they write it. Never infer it.

slots.ask: Do you have a website of your own?
Do you have a square photo or logo for your profile picture?
slots.write: The member uploads it in the editor; never fetch one from the web.

slots.ask: What role are you looking for, where, and from when? What are you best at?
slots.write: Bold-labelled lines as in the sample. Never mention salary, health, family or immigration status unless they insist.

slots.ask: What roles have you had? For each: years, title, employer and one result you're proud of.
slots.write: tag = years; title = role · employer; description = one result, with a number only if they give it. Newest first. No links needed.

slots.ask: Do you have case studies or work samples you can share publicly?
slots.write: Only work cleared for public sharing. They upload any pictures.

slots.ask: How should recruiters reach you? Do you have a CV link?
slots.write: Email: Only an address they confirm may be public: everyone can see it. A CV link only to a file they host and are happy to make public.

slots.ask: Which professional profiles should be linked?
